title: Cartograph CLI output, contract 1.0
description: The document emitted by `cartograph --json`, `cartograph trace --json`, and the per-stage commands. Every edge carries the case for believing it; an edge serialised as only its endpoints is not a Cartograph edge.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract. Minor for additive changes; major for anything a consumer could break on.

repository.description: What was analysed. Never an absolute filesystem path: a graph states facts about a repository, not about the machine that analysed it.

requested.description: The path as typed, when relative. A rooted path — absolute, or Windows drive-less — is replaced by the literal `<absolute>`.

summary.description: Counts, in the vocabulary the human summary uses: observed, resolved, refused. Never 'verified'.

symbols.description: Declared symbols across every parsed file.

routes_observed.description: Route declarations found in source. An observation, not an endpoint.

http_observed.description: Syntactically HTTP-looking call sites. An observation, not a relationship.

tables_resolved.description: Models that resolved to a table name.

cross_language_edges.description: Edges whose endpoints were extracted by different grammars.

client_call_edges.description: Calls into a function that issues a request.

ambiguous.description: Observations with rival candidates. No edge is produced; this is by design.

files_failed.description: Files that could not be parsed at all. Non-zero means the graph is missing whatever they contained.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds for extraction, resolution and construction.

nodes.description: Every node in the produced graph, in id order.

id.description: Stable within one run. Referenced by edge source and target.

file.description: Repository-relative, forward slashes. Absent when the node has no source location.

edges.description: Every edge in the produced graph, in id order. Cartograph never stores `A -> B`: the four attributes below are required by the domain model and an edge without them does not compile, let alone serialise.

confidence.description: The specification's prior for this evidence class. UNCALIBRATED: not a measured probability. See docs/benchmarks/m08-confidence-policy.md.

provenance.description: Which analysis produced the edge. `model-inference` is a statistical classifier, never a language model (RULE 007).

evidence.description: A structural description of the observation. Never source text (RULE 015).

file.description: Repository-relative path where the claim was observed.

line.description: One-based line where the claim was observed.

diagnostics.description: Parse problems. Recoverable unless summary.files_failed is non-zero.

message.description: Structural metadata only. Never source text.

errors.description: Failures. Present and empty on success, so a consumer checks one field unconditionally. A run that failed before producing a graph emits a document with only schema_version, command and errors.

message.description: One sentence, addressed to the person who ran the command.

hint.description: The next action, when there is an obvious one.

result.description: The command-specific section. Present only for `trace`; omitted rather than emitted empty, so a consumer can tell 'this command produces no traces' from 'this trace found nothing'.

from.description: The node the walk started from.

steps.description: The hops, each carrying the edge traversed and the node it led to. Nested through `next`.

reaches_table.description: Whether any branch reached a database table — the full cross-stack chain.

stop.description: Why the walk stopped, when it stopped immediately.
